title: Database as a Work Queue
pattern: Using a relational database table to store task/job states and repeatedly polling and updating row statuses to distribute work among application instances.
why_bad: Relational databases are not designed for queueing. High-frequency updates and row locking (`FOR UPDATE`) cause extreme lock contention, deadlocks, and index bloat. As the table grows, query performance drops off a cliff, leading to thread blocking and cascading failures [273, 274, 565, 566].
detection: Frequent queries executed with `FOR UPDATE` combined with status columns (e.g., `PENDING`, `DONE`) being constantly updated in tight loops.
counterexample: ACID transactional updates where row locking is transient and not used to distribute long-running background jobs.
fix: Move queueing semantics to dedicated message brokers (e.g., RabbitMQ, Kafka) designed for asynchronous, low-latency, non-blocking message passing [530, 562].
source:
*Pragmatic Programmers - Release It! (Nygard), p. 177-178 [273, 274, 565, 566]*  
*Implementing Domain-Driven Design (Vernon), p. 312 [530]*
